taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts Liatris punctata with three varieties, including var. punctata and var. mucronata. Liatris mucronata DC. is a synonym of Liatris punctata var. mucronata. Project counting stays at one canonical species, with local varieties taught inside the learner.

evidence: Hays — Purola Preserve explicitly documents both Liatris punctata and the familiar Liatris mucronata concept.
Travis — UT work on the Hays/Travis distribution of the two local varieties documents the complex in Travis County.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed local treatment of Liatris punctata var. mucronata.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Species-level PASS reflects explicit county evidence for the accepted species complex; no duplicate count is created for the synonym Liatris mucronata.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the stem and corm if you need to separate the local varieties. In north Hays material, var. mucronata tends to have glossy reddish stems and a smaller, more spherical corm, while var. punctata tends to have grayer, more pubescent stems and larger, hairier achenes. Both belong to the same canonical Liatris punctata species in this learner.
diagnostic_traits: unbranched terminal spikelike array of sessile discoid heads
heads with only a few purple florets
local var. mucronata often glossy reddish-stemmed; var. punctata grayer and more pubescent in north Hays material

local_variety_lesson.Liatris punctata var. mucronata: accepted variety; former/familiar Liatris mucronata; reddish glossy stems common locally; smaller more spheroid corm in the Hays comparison
local_variety_lesson.Liatris punctata var. punctata: accepted autonym variety; grayer more pubescent stems common locally; larger corm and larger hairier achenes in the Hays comparison
